w10.001: A Chronology of the Local Universe
w10.002: Appendix IX The Chronology of Local Universes (pp. 293–306)
w10.003: The preceding appendices set out the principles of experiential growth; this one watches those principles unfold, step by step, in the life of a single local universe. Sadler takes Nebadon, the universe The Urantia Book describes most fully, as his sample, and gathers dates scattered across the Papers into one continuous line running from the first alteration of space potency to the distant future of light and life. Physical organization, the creation of life, the bestowals and the rebellions, and the stages through which Son and Spirit pass together become a single long narrative.
w10.004: 1. Before the Nebula: The Primary Force Organizers (orig. pp. 293–295)
w10.005: Where does the history of a local universe begin? Sadler suspects that even Uversa held no record of Nebadon's remotest physical origins, since the Uversa Council of Equilibrium had to be informed separately when conditions in some region of space became favorable for materialization. Such records, he reasons, would more likely lie in the Paradise archives of the Master Architects, for it is the Master Architects who plan material creation and oversee the primary force organizers.
w10.006: He reduces the prehistory of the Andronover nebula to three movements. First, perhaps well over a trillion years ago, part of the Unqualified Absolute's space potency underwent a change so that it could respond to the mere presence of primary force organizers. Second, when those organizers later entered that sector of Orvonton, their passive presence alone was enough to turn the space potency into primordial force. Third, after a further interval, they took up the active work of transmuting primordial force into primary, or puissant, energy.
w10.008: At this stage the star students of neighboring universes could detect nothing at all. Anything a human observer would call mass appears only after the ultimatonic stage, when electrons and atoms come into being.
w10.009: The result is an intriguing scene. The primary force organizers go out from Paradise and work without the knowledge of the superuniverse authorities, who only later "discover" what they have done. Some 987 billion years ago an associate force organizer serving as acting inspector of Orvonton came upon the Andronover pre-nebula and reported it to the Ancients of Days [57:1.3]. Then, 900 billion years ago, the Uversa Council of Equilibrium granted permission to begin materialization [57:1.4]. Sadler reads the date of this permit as the boundary at which jurisdiction passed from the primary force organizers of Paradise to the associate force organizers of Uversa.
w10.010: 2. The Birth of the Nebula and Its Power Workers (orig. pp. 295–298)
w10.011: The era of the associate force organizers
w10.012: Once the permit was issued, its discoverer left Uversa with his staff, and 875 billion years ago the Andronover nebula was formally initiated. The way a nebula is set spinning is surprisingly simple.
w10.014: The force organizers move off at right angles to the plane of the disk they mean to set turning. Sadler takes the designation 876,926 to be the nebula's serial number within Orvonton. The associate force organizers convert puissant energy into gravity energy, and ultimatons are born. In outer space they stay with a nebula to the end, but within a superuniverse the custom is for them to withdraw at a certain point and hand the work over to the power centers and physical controllers of the region.
w10.016: Sadler describes the physical evolution of a local universe as the technical challenge accepted by the power centers and physical controllers. Their task is to bring matter into balance and to show that mind can master energy. He thinks that every power center eventually assigned to Nebadon (100 of local-universe rank, 1,000 of constellation rank, 10,000 of system rank) may have come to Andronover from the start, and from the 500,000 master physical controllers of Satania he arrives at roughly five billion for the whole local universe. Both figures are estimates.
w10.017: These beings worked alone from about 875 billion years ago until the Creator Son arrived 400 billion years ago. During that span energy was organized from the ultimatonic stage, through the electronic stage, into atomic matter. When gross mass appeared about 800 billion years ago, neighboring creations became aware of it through gravity measurements. The nebula then drew in energy until it reached its maximum mass, and with the birth of its first sun 500 billion years ago it entered the spiral phase of outward dispersal. It was during this second phase that Michael arrived together with the Creative Spirit.
w10.018: The chronology of Andronover and Nebadon: successive jurisdictions and major events (the time axis is not to scale)
w10.019: 3. The Arrival of Michael and the Creative Spirit (orig. pp. 298–301)
w10.021: Michael reached the Andronover region 400 billion years ago [119:0.7]. His training as a universe administrator had already been completed in the central universe, and the Spirit who was to become his consort had received preliminary training for creatorship under the circuit Spirits of Havona. His authority was granted by the Paradise Trinity and confirmed by the Master Spirit of Orvonton.
w10.023: The word "leasehold" deserves reflection. A Creator Son does not arrive as owner of his universe. Like a tenant handed a parcel of land, he must cultivate it and, through the experience gained there, earn his sovereignty for himself. Upon his arrival the power centers and physical controllers began building Salvington, the capital, together with the hundred constellation headquarters; not until five billion years ago were all the system headquarters finished [57:3.8].
w10.024: The Creative Spirit sets the boundary
w10.025: The coming of the Creative Spirit fixed the boundary of the local universe. Whatever lies within the region of space she recognizes as her own is Nebadon; whatever lies outside it is not [41:0.1]. How many nebulae, then, fall within that region? Here Sadler attempts a calculation.
w10.026: Andronover gave birth to 1,013,628 suns [57:4.8]. Sadler uses the distribution of inhabited worlds in Satania as his yardstick.
w10.028: Sadler's two estimates of the number of nebulae
w10.032: Either way, Andronover alone cannot supply the ten million inhabited worlds planned for Nebadon. The Papers themselves say that Nebadon was assembled from the offspring of several nebulae [41:0.3]. Because nebulae differ in size, no exact count is possible.
w10.034: How, then, did nebulae of different origin come to orbit together as the single Nebadon star cloud? Sadler names four factors: a minimum of shared space motion among the nebulae from the outset; intelligent adjustment by the power centers and physical controllers; the matter-controlling attributes of the Creator Son; and the space presence and physical powers of the Creative Spirit, antigravity among them. He pictures the Spirit in this era as a kind of "super-power center."
w10.036: In this period the Son supplied the pattern and the Spirit turned it into physical substance [34:0.3]. Their only counselors were the 1,000 Tertiaphim given by the Infinite Spirit. Three hundred billion years ago Michael's staff arrived at Salvington, and the government of Uversa recognized Nebadon as a physical creation [57:3.9].
w10.037: 4. Life Creation and a Universe of Inhabitation (orig. pp. 301–304)
w10.039: The Papers do not say when the life-creation era began. All that is certain is that it came after Michael's arrival 400 billion years ago and before the oldest inhabited worlds appeared 200 billion years ago. As in other appendices, Sadler takes the midpoint, roughly 300 billion years ago.
w10.040: With the opening of this era the status of Son and Spirit changes together. The Son moves into associate vicegerent sovereignty, and the Spirit acquires personal attributes and becomes the Universe Mother Spirit. This personalization is a gift of Paradise Deity bestowed through the Master Spirit of Orvonton [17:6.7]. From then on the Spirit leaves the work of physical organization behind and functions as a spiritual creator and as the source of local universe mind.
w10.041: Creation proceeds from Gabriel, the Bright and Morning Star, to the Father Melchizedek and the Melchizedek order, then to the Vorondadeks, the Lanonandeks, the Life Carriers, the Brilliant Evening Stars, the Archangels, and the Susatia and Univitatia. After these the Son alone produces the Adams and Eves of the systems, and the Spirit alone brings forth the angelic hosts. Sadler stresses that what holds such a universe together is neither the Spirit's presence alone nor mere physical cohesion. A vast network of communication lines, energy circuits, and power lanes welds it into a single administrative unit [41:1.1].
w10.043: Two hundred billion years ago the oldest inhabited worlds came into being, and Nebadon rose to a new level.
w10.045: Meanwhile the physical evolution of Andronover went on. Beginning 75 billion years ago, suns were produced in great numbers over fifty billion years, and between eight and six billion years ago the nebula passed through its final eruptions. Sadler raises a question here: when the last upheavals came, a good many worlds must already have been inhabited; were their peoples carried to new worlds by the technique of dematerialization [51:2.3]? The Papers are silent on the matter.
w10.046: Our own sun came into being six billion years ago, toward the end of that last disruption. Urantia's own history began about a billion years ago, life was planted 550 million years ago, and human beings appeared about a million years ago, when the planet was registered as world number 606 of Satania.
w10.047: 5. Bestowals, Rebellions, and the Stages of Sovereignty (orig. pp. 304–306)
w10.049: Michael's bestowal era began about a billion years ago.
w10.051: Sadler sets this span beside the two hundred billion years that have passed since the oldest inhabited worlds. The bestowal era amounts to half of one percent of that time, the equivalent of about six weeks in a human life of a hundred years. Yet all three system rebellions in Nebadon fall within it: the Palonia rebellion about 850 million years ago, the rebellion in system 87 of constellation 61 about 600 million years ago, and the Lucifer rebellion in Satania two hundred thousand years ago. Sadler thinks the second must be the uprising in which Lanaforge, as assistant System Sovereign, took over the reins of government [45:2.3].
w10.052: Why should a universe that knew no system rebellion for two hundred billion years experience three within a single billion? Sadler wonders whether the bestowal era might be a final test, a season of temporary instability that a local universe passes through before reaching settled sovereignty. Yet he candidly adds that while he is sure the two facts are meaningfully related, he does not know what that relation is.
w10.054: The Urantia Book divides both the sovereignty of a Creator Son [21:3.5–11] and the career of a Universe Mother Spirit [17:6.3–10] into seven stages. Set side by side and fitted to Sadler's chronology, they look like this.
w10.055: Stages of the Creator Son's sovereignty and of the Creative Spirit's career (Nebadon)
w10.059: bestowal era, from about a billion years ago
w10.060: from a little over 1,900 years ago
w10.061: when most worlds are settled in light and life
w10.062: when the whole local universe is settled
w10.064: The moment when Michael, having finished his seventh bestowal, enters supreme sovereignty is also the point at which the two careers meet.
w10.066: How far away is light and life?
w10.067: The postbestowal history of Nebadon is not yet two thousand years old. By the most recent registry the universe has 3,840,101 inhabited worlds, under forty percent of the ten million planned [32:2.9]. Satania is somewhat further along with 619, about sixty-two percent of its quota. Adding the thirty-six planets awaiting life implantation and the nearly two hundred expected to be ready within a few million years brings the total to roughly 850 [49:0.3]. Judging by the pace of the past two hundred billion years, Sadler estimates that life implantation will continue for hundreds of billions of years to come, so that the settling of all Nebadon in light and life is far from imminent.
w10.069: In one place Sadler writes "Polonia" for the first rebel system, but the Papers spell it Palonia [119:2.5]. The average of 1.09363 he gives for the distribution of worlds in Satania does not match 619 divided by 562 (about 1.10); since he immediately rounds to 1.1 for his calculation, however, the conclusion is unaffected. The figure of some two thousand suns, which he attributes to 41:2.1, is not found there but in 41:3.1.
w10.070: Taking Nebadon as his sample, Sadler threads the history of a local universe into a single chronology, from the alteration of space potency to light and life.
w10.071: Before the nebula, the primary force organizers work out from Paradise; with the permit of 900 billion years ago, jurisdiction passes to the associate force organizers of Uversa.
w10.072: After Andronover was initiated 875 billion years ago, the power centers and physical controllers guided physical evolution alone until Michael and the Creative Spirit arrived 400 billion years ago.
w10.073: The space presence of the Creative Spirit determines the boundary of the local universe; by Sadler's reckoning Nebadon needs somewhere between nine and twenty nebulae the size of Andronover.
w10.074: With the era of life creation the Son enters associate vicegerent sovereignty and the Spirit her personal stage; 200 billion years ago Nebadon was registered as a universe of mortal ascension.
w10.075: All three system rebellions fell within a bestowal era of little more than a billion years; Sadler senses a meaningful connection but leaves its nature open.
w10.076: The Son's seven stages of sovereignty and the Spirit's seven career stages run in parallel, and Nebadon now stands at the very beginning of supreme sovereignty.
w10.078: Appendix X The First Experiential Trinity (pp. 307–322)
w10.079: The Paradise Trinity is existential; the Ultimate Trinity is experiential. This new Trinity already functions as a qualified reality, but it will be factually formed only when the evolution of the Supreme Being is complete. Counting its members, Sadler finds more than 1.4 million personalities involved, and he argues that this very size forces precise thinking about what a trinity is. His conclusion is that a trinity is not a partnership of persons but a corporative union of Deities, and that the corps of Architects and the corps of Supreme Creators will therefore each take part as a single Deity entity.
w10.080: 1. One Being and Two Groups (orig. pp. 307–308)
w10.081: The membership of the Ultimate Trinity is given in the Foreword of The Urantia Book.
w10.083: At first sight it appears threefold, as the other two Trinities are. In the Paradise Trinity we find the Father, the Son, and the Spirit; in the Absolute Trinity, God the Supreme, God the Ultimate, and the Consummator of Universe Destiny. Yet this "middle Trinity" is different: it is formed not of three beings but of one being and two groups. Sadler actually counts the numbers.
w10.084: Personalities involved in the Ultimate Trinity (Sadler's count)
w10.093: How can nearly a million and a half personalities function within one trinity? Sadler finds this startling number useful. Because the Paradise Trinity has three members, we tend to blur the personal partnership of Father, Son, and Spirit (a triunity) with the Trinity itself; faced with more than 1.4 million members, such confusion becomes impossible.
w10.096: Sadler gathers what the Papers say about the Paradise Trinity and builds his argument on the premise that the same principles will hold for other trinities. He begins with the triunity.
w10.100: Sadler translates the difference into the language of human affairs. A triunity resembles a partnership or an association; a trinity resembles a corporation. A corporation is not a person, yet it is unmistakably an entity. In this spirit he playfully names the Paradise Trinity "Undivided Deity, Incorporated."
w10.101: The First Triunity and the Paradise Trinity
w10.103: personal association of Father, Son, and Spirit
Deity union of Father, Son, and Spirit
w10.105: love, mercy, ministry; bestowal of personality, spirit, and mind
administration of justice, totality attitudes, cosmic overcontrol
w10.106: whole planets, whole universes, the entire grand universe
w10.107: The two sets of functions do not overlap. Goodness, mercy, and truth are ministered one by one by the divine persons, but justice is not the attitude of any single one of them.
w10.110: A trinity is not a person, yet neither does it run counter to personality. Its personal aspects reside in its individual members, and those members, taken one by one, are not the trinity.
w10.112: Sadler compares this to the board of a corporation. The directors may lead their own lives quite apart from the company, and the company, as a legal entity, exists independently of their private affairs. But the directors cannot act together "as directors" outside the company. Whether a trinity has three members or a million, its organic structure is an entity distinct from its individual members.
w10.114: The key to the discussion is a single sentence in Paper 106.
w10.116: From this Sadler draws a decisive inference. If the corps of Supreme Creators and the corps of Master Architects join in the Ultimate Trinity, they must do so not as multitudes of personalities but as two corporative Deity entities. Moreover, since trinity function always embraces Deity reality, and Deity reality always seeks personalization [0:12.4], a new personalization of Deity arises as the consequence of trinity. This is why experiential Deity appears in the universe.
w10.118: The Deity of the Supreme Being
w10.119: The figure of 1.4 million counted above is not, strictly speaking, the number of members. According to Sadler the Ultimate Trinity has just three members, not one of which is a personality. The first is comparatively easy to grasp. When the second universe age has ended and His evolution is complete, the Supreme Being takes part not as a person but as Deity. The member is the Deity of Supremacy, not the personality of God the Supreme.
w10.120: The Deity of the Architect corps
w10.121: The second member is less familiar. The Architects are 28,011 superpersonal beings, yet the trinity has only one "Architect member." That member must therefore be some Deity entity that stands for, or unites, the whole corps' superpersonal spirit, its absonite divinity, and its purpose for the master universe. Sadler states plainly that this is a new concept about which the Papers say nothing; he holds only that it is the one concept consistent with the known facts. If such an entity needed a "voice," one might imagine the senior Master Architect speaking for it, much as the chairman speaks for a board.
w10.122: The Deity of the Supreme Creator corps
w10.123: The third member is harder still. The Architect corps has existed from the beginning, but the corps of Supreme Creators is an evolving group, originating in time and not yet complete. How might its Deity entity come into being? With almost no guidance from the text, Sadler leans on logic and assembles his clues.
w10.124: The first clue is a phrase from the Foreword's introduction of the Supreme Being.
w10.126: Sadler believes the words "triune Paradise Deity" were chosen with deliberate breadth, signaling that the Supreme Creators do not always stand in one and the same relation to Paradise Deity. The Reflective Spirits, for instance, were created through a liaison of the Paradise Trinity with a single Master Spirit [17:2.1], which is the personal collaboration of one Master Spirit. Yet the seven Master Spirits can also unite as a sevenfold Deity union and so become associated with trinity function.
w10.128: Here Sadler poses a question. Might this corporative Deity union of the Master Spirits foreshadow the eventual appearance of a Deity entity that unites the divinity of the Supreme Creator corps as a whole? And if the Supreme Creators achieve a "⟦Q 116:2.13⟧unification of divine power and personality⟦/Q⟧" [116:2.13], might that unification yield, besides power, a coalescence of divinity as well?
w10.129: His conclusion runs as follows. As the Supreme Creators jointly evolve the Almighty's power, they are likely bringing forth at the same time a new Deity entity for the corps as a whole. This would not be a personalization of the corps but a Deity unity projected beyond it. Sadler supposes that its attributes, like those of the Master Spirits, would bear a supreme, ultimate, and supreme-ultimate character. He calls this entity "Consolidated Supreme Creators, Incorporated," and for its voice he thinks of Master Spirit Number Seven, who speaks for the sevenfold Deity union. As warrant for such conjecture he notes that the Papers themselves encourage creative speculation.
w10.130: The three members of the Ultimate Trinity: three Deity entities raised above groups of personalities (the two dashed boxes are Sadler's inference)
w10.131: Seen this way, the members of the Ultimate Trinity are accurately named as follows: Supreme Being Deity, Master Architect corps Deity, and Supreme Creator corps Deity. In the same way, the Paradise Trinity, strictly speaking, joins Father Deity, Son Deity, and Spirit Deity.
w10.133: The Ultimate Trinity is not yet fully real, yet it would be wrong to call it unreal.
w10.135: Sadler describes it as a reality in the process of becoming. Even now it functions in a limited way, and its range is widening. The Papers indicate that the mobilization of the seven corps of finality may represent a present activity of the Ultimate Trinity [31:10.10]. Its future function is clearer.
w10.137: The Paradise Trinity co-ordinates the ultimate as a self-qualified absolute. Sadler expects that in the post-Supreme ages the function of the Ultimate Trinity will expand until, so far as absonite reality is concerned, it supplements and perhaps replaces the co-ordination of the Paradise Trinity.
w10.138: Because the Ultimate Trinity is composed of derived Deities and is not infinite, it can be completely unified.
w10.140: Sadler summarizes its goals as three: co-ordinating the master universe as a whole, the experiential unification of the Trinity itself, and the power-personalization of God the Ultimate. He then proposes a theory that these three goals advance together through four stages, matching the successive conquest of the four outer space levels, and are reached all at once when the sixth universe age ends, when the Quartan Space Level is settled. He acknowledges that the Papers do not describe how this will come about.
w10.142: In Sadler's table the total of 1,428,040 includes the Supreme Being and the 28,011 Architects, yet later he sometimes uses the same figure as though it were the membership of the Supreme Creator corps alone; counted by itself, that corps numbers 1,400,028. In the passage on the Architect member, "the second experiential trinity" is clearly a slip for the first. And the reference given for comparing the evolution of the Almighty with the appearance of the Conjoint Actor, 116:2.15, does not exist; the content is found in 116:2.14.
w10.144: Why the whole exceeds the sum of its parts
w10.145: Both trinity and triunity possess functions that cannot be predicted from the sum of their members' attributes [104:3.17]. Sadler looks for the reason in pattern and system. Between two objects there can be only a relationship, but when three or more come together, a system emerges [112:1.17].
w10.147: Sadler calls this "shape of the whole" by the German word Gestalt and illustrates it with three coins. Drop three coins on a table and they will usually form some irregular triangle. Set them at equal distances, however, and they form an equilateral triangle, and now each coin has a "positional value." That value comes from no single coin; it arises from each coin's relation to the whole. He makes the same point with nine strangers who wander onto a baseball diamond, as against nine players of a team that knows how to work together.
w10.148: Aggregate and system: three coins dropped at random and three coins placed at equal distances
w10.150: If both possess a Gestalt, why is a triunity a partnership and a trinity a corporation? Sadler finds the answer in the nature of personality.
w10.152: Personality can be neither subtracted nor added. Deity, by contrast, can be added. Sadler speaks of a kind of plasticity in Deity that personality does not have. He therefore concludes that Deity employs two techniques of self-realization at once, opposite in direction yet complementary. Personality expression unifies the parts inwardly; trinity formation unifies the whole outwardly. The one expresses individuality, the other totality.
w10.154: Sadler holds that whenever three Deities function on the same level of reality, a system results, and within that system a trinity must appear. The bond is divinity, that quality of Deity which unifies and co-ordinates [0:1.16]. He then carries the principle one step further. The Paradise Trinity and the Ultimate Trinity, being two, can only be related; but once a third trinity appears, the three trinities in turn form a system, and the result is the Trinity of Trinities.
w10.155: The Ultimate Trinity is the first experiential Trinity, whose members are the Supreme Being, the Supreme Creators, and the Master Architects. It is now a qualified reality and will be factually formed after the evolution of the Supreme Being is complete.
w10.156: More than 1.4 million personalities are involved, but Sadler sees this number as an aid to thinking precisely about what a trinity is.
w10.157: A triunity is a partnership of persons; a trinity is a corporative entity of Deities. Only the deified can become trinity.
w10.158: Sadler infers that each of the two corps, Architects and Supreme Creators, will take part in the Trinity as a single corporative Deity entity. This is his interpretation of matters on which the Papers are silent.
w10.159: The Ultimate Trinity co-ordinates the transcendental, and its function will grow in the post-Supreme ages; its complete unification leads to the power-personalization of God the Ultimate.
w10.160: A system exceeds the sum of its parts because its parts are arranged and carry positional value. Sadler calls this a Gestalt.
w10.161: Personalities are associable but not totalable. Through personality expression and trinity formation, Deity achieves both individuality and totality.
w10.164: The post-Supreme ages are the third through the sixth universe ages, in which the four outer space levels open one after another. In this appendix Sadler gathers what the Papers reveal and what may reasonably be conjectured, sketching Havona, the superuniverses, and Nebadon in the coming age, the collaboration of two Trinities, new functions of the Supreme Being, and the role of the finaliters. Beneath it all lies his earlier idea of a nuclear universe and cytoplasmic universes: the finite experience that the outer universes lack becomes the opportunity for service by the citizens of the grand universe.
w10.165: 1. The Third Age in the Grand Universe (orig. pp. 323–327)
w10.166: Sadler expects the coming ages to be marked by three great movements: an outward thrust of grand universe personalities into outer space; a search for God the Ultimate, who emerges in those ages; and an inward thrust of outer beings passing through the superuniverses and Havona toward Paradise in quest of the Universal Father as Ultimate.
w10.169: Havona, into which evolution entered with the arrival of Grandfanda, will change again in the third age. The Papers confess that they do not fully understand why a Universal Censor is stationed on each of Havona's billion spheres, and they suggest that this may anticipate some future age when Havona's population could change [19:4.2]. Havona may also become a training universe for absonite beings.
w10.171: Sadler's reasoning runs like this. If in the second age Havona, through contact with the imperfect superuniverses, broke through the limits of its inherent perfection to gain finite experiential growth, then in the third age it will gain a new kind of growth, superfinite or absonite in character.
w10.173: Sadler imagines that just as "quiet zones" separate the space levels, so "quiet times" may separate the universe ages, intervals in which the great changes attending the emergence of the Supreme Being can become fully consolidated. If so, by the dawn of the third age the superuniverses will long since have been settled in light and life. The Papers make clear that such settlement is not the end.
w10.175: As superuniverse boundaries fall away, there will also be "lateral growth," as the culture of Orvonton mingles with that of the other six superuniverses. Sadler sees this as the post-Supreme synthesis of the diversity first imprinted by the Seven Master Spirits.
w10.177: Sadler's speculations about Nebadon are bold. The Universe Son and Spirit have gone out into outer space, and Nebadon is no longer a creative unit but an administrative one. He imagines a regency commission of Gabriel, the Father Melchizedek, and perhaps the Union of Days, ruling in Michael's name. The place of the Solitary Messengers is taken by the Inspired Trinity Spirits [19:5.4].
w10.178: Natives of Nebadon born in the third age will have no finite experience at all. Sadler thinks that "mortals" of that time might bypass death and become first-stage spirits at once, skipping the morontia career entirely. With the Creator Son and Creative Spirit gone, Son-fusion and Spirit-fusion would be difficult, leaving only Adjuster fusion. He concludes that some new path of ascension will open. And as outer space opens more widely, he foresees a swelling tide of incoming pilgrims that will eventually far outnumber the native population of the grand universe.
w10.179: The post-Supreme ages: a current flowing out from the inner universes and a current flowing in from the outer universes
w10.180: 2. Two Trinities in Outer Space (orig. pp. 327–328)
w10.181: For the first time in master universe history, two Trinities will work side by side. Sadler draws two distinctions between them. When the Paradise Trinity acts, an existential Trinity is qualifying its own absoluteness. The action of the Ultimate Trinity is experiential and involves no such qualification, since absonite reality is dealing with absonite reality. He conjectures that as the function of the Ultimate Trinity broadens and its unity deepens, the function of the Paradise Trinity will recede accordingly.
w10.182: 3. The Supreme Being in the Inner and Outer Universes (orig. pp. 328–330)
w10.183: To speak of the coming ages Sadler uses the terms "inner universes" and "outer universes." Concerning the functions of the Supreme Being the Papers say:
w10.185: The same paragraph sets out three conjectures side by side: that the third function will involve the third level of Deity manifestation; that the Supreme will expand in power as the superalmighty of the outer universes; and the unknown mind potential itself. Sadler interprets the first as participation, together with God the Absolute, in the second experiential Trinity, and the second as the extension of present superuniverse sovereignty to the outer creations. On the third he gathers the passages about the mind of Supremacy, bestowed by the Conjoint Actor and focalized in Majeston.
w10.187: The growth of body and spirit reaches its limit on worlds settled in light and life, but the growth of mind has no end. Sadler expects the Supreme Being to be active in all three domains: as a spirit personality in Havona, as almighty sovereign in the grand universe, and through some new function of mind across the whole master universe.
w10.188: 4. Spirit and Supremacy, God the Sevenfold, and the Finaliters (orig. pp. 330–333)
w10.189: Dual Deity on the creative frontier
w10.190: Sadler revisits a principle from Appendix V: partnerships of dual Deity work on the frontiers of creation, and once a frontier is settled they hand it over to administrators of Trinity origin. The Father-Son partnership opened the first age and entrusted Havona to Trinity administration. The Son-Spirit partnership, having perfected seven hundred thousand local universes in the second age, will make way for administrators of Trinity origin [23:4.4]. What, then, is the next partnership?
w10.192: Sadler surmises that in outer space a new partnership will appear between the Infinite Spirit and the Supreme Being, one that may include the Master Spirits and perhaps even the Creative Spirits. Even now the Infinite Spirit compensates in many ways for the incompleteness of the Supreme Being, and Master Spirit Number Seven speaks for the Supreme. Still, he admits that he cannot picture this partnership in detail. The expansion of God the Sevenfold is treated separately in Appendices XII–XIV.
w10.194: Many beings besides the finaliters will serve in the outer universes. The close ties forming among Creator Sons, Creative Spirits, Brilliant Evening Stars, Teacher Sons, and finaliters suggest that they will work together in outer space [55:10.9]. Sadler conjectures that the Magisterial Sons and the Mighty Messengers will someday join their ranks.
w10.195: The finaliters themselves are not yet fully grown.
w10.197: Of the seven dimensions of personality, we now develop only the three on the finite level; the three on the absonite level are held in reserve for future growth [112:1.9]. Sadler therefore says that most of our growth will take place after the age of the Supreme, and that the Paradise ascent and finaliter service in the grand universe are, seen in the larger view, only a kind of kindergarten beginning.
w10.198: The bond between the finaliters and the Supreme Being grows ever closer. On attaining the seventh stage of spirit existence, the mortal mind and the Adjuster mind unite with the experiential mind of the Supreme to form a triune mind [117:5.3].
w10.200: 5. Cytoplasmic Need Enlarges Nuclear Function (orig. pp. 333–334)
w10.201: Sadler closes this appendix with the concept of nuclear and cytoplasmic universes from Chapter IV of his main text. In relation to outer space, the grand universe is the nucleus and the outer universes are the cytoplasm. What the cytoplasm lacks, what the outer universes do not possess, is finite experience.
w10.203: The peoples of the grand universe bear the essence of the Supreme Being within their own experiential nature, and that is precisely the element missing in outer space. The finaliters come truly to know the Supreme Being and are destined to serve and reveal this Supreme Deity in the outer universes of the future [56:8.2].
w10.204: Sadler points out that the same pattern of relationship exists in the present age. We human beings lack the divine perfection of the beings of Havona and Paradise, yet our very imperfection and need give them an opportunity to serve, and through that service they pass beyond the walls of growth that their created perfection had set around them. As the Havoners now grow by ministering to us, so in the next age we shall grow by ministering to the beings of outer space. That in every age the inhabitants of the age before outgrow their former limits is the principle Sadler returns to again and again in this appendix.
w10.205: The post-Supreme ages are the third through sixth universe ages, in which the four outer space levels open; an outgoing current and an incoming current flow at the same time.
w10.206: Sadler expects Havona to gain absonite growth in the third age, a second transformation, and the superuniverses to pass beyond the limits of light and life and to mingle with one another.
w10.207: After the Creators depart, Nebadon becomes an administrative unit; Sadler imagines a regency commission centered on Gabriel and the Father Melchizedek. This is his conjecture.
w10.208: For the first time two Trinities function together, and Sadler surmises that as the function of the Ultimate Trinity grows, that of the Paradise Trinity will recede.
w10.209: The Papers call the third function of the Supreme an unknown mind potential; Sadler anticipates all three aspects: the third level of Deity manifestation, the superalmighty, and a new function of mind.
w10.210: After Father-Son and Son-Spirit comes the Spirit-Supreme partnership, and Sadler expects this new dual-Deity relationship to appear on the frontier of outer space.
w10.211: The finaliters have not yet attained ultimate spirit status; compared with post-Supreme growth, the ascent so far is a kind of kindergarten.
w10.212: The finite experience the outer universes lack becomes an opportunity for grand universe citizens to serve: cytoplasmic need enlarges nuclear function.
w11.001: The Widening of God the Sevenfold
w11.002: Appendix XII, Expansion of God the Sevenfold (pp. 335–339)
w11.003: The Urantia Book devotes only a single sentence to the matter: the function of God the Sevenfold “will probably expand” as outer space evolves. Sadler takes hold of that sentence and asks three questions. Does God the Sevenfold have a mind aspect as well? How will the work of the Supreme Creators widen in outer space? Could the seven levels become ten? Since nearly everything in this appendix is Sadler's own reasoning, it must be read alongside the passages on which that reasoning leans.
w11.004: 1. The Sentence That Starts It All (orig. p. 335)
w11.006: The same paragraph adds that the future universes on the primary through quartan levels of outer space will witness the inauguration of a transcendent and absonite approach to Deity. Sadler reads the word “expand” in two senses. The first is an expansion in quantity: God the Sevenfold carries His work beyond the grand universe into outer space. The second is an expansion in quality. If the present seven levels form a ladder suited to finite creatures, might an absonite approach not require additional rungs? The text clearly implies only the first; the second is a question Sadler himself opens.
w11.007: 2. God the Sevenfold Today: Two Series and a Possible Third (orig. pp. 335–336)
w11.008: The Urantia Book presents God the Sevenfold not only as a ladder of spiritual ministry. In Paper 116 it also shows a “sevenfold” order of controllers that upholds the physical structure of the grand universe.
w11.010: The two series of God the Sevenfold (counted from the bottom)
w11.019: On Sadler's account the two series are joined at three points. Existentially they are already one in the Universal Father and the Conjoint Actor. Experientially they are becoming one as the Almighty and the Supreme are united through the Supreme Mind. Functionally they meet in the cooperation of the Seven Master Spirits with the Seven Supreme Power Directors.
w11.020: The text says that man finds in the Sevenfold its “personal and spiritual divinity,” yet adds that there are other phases unconcerned with the progress of personality [106:1.4]. If the sevenfold controllers form one such phase, might there not be a series of mind as well? Sadler tries to fill seven places, rising from the Master Physical Controllers (pre-adjutant mind) through the adjutant mind-spirits, the Creative Spirits, the Seven Master Spirits (cosmic mind), Majeston, and the Conjoint Actor, up to the Father-Son. He himself says this series is not essential to his argument, so it is best taken as a tentative arrangement that matches the threefold division of spirit, mind, and matter.
w11.021: 3. Where Will the Supreme Creators Go? (orig. pp. 336–338)
w11.022: There is no doubt that God the Supreme, together with the three Deities of Paradise, will be engaged in outer space. The open question concerns the three lower levels of God the Sevenfold, and the text itself leaves it open.
w11.024: The same paragraph observes that as the creations become settled, the first three manifestations of God the Sevenfold withdraw. Sadler takes this to mean that those who withdraw from the present age move on into the next. The Seven Master Spirits will remain in the grand universe, yet because the plans even of the “correlative segments of outer space” were conditioned by their diversity [16:0.11], their influence will reach there as well (see Appendix XIV). The Ancients of Days appear likely to stay in the superuniverses as vicegerents of the Supreme, caring for the outer-space dwellers who will pass through the superuniverses on their way into Havona [56:7.9]. The creators most plainly headed for outer space are the two creators of the local universe. Sadler expects three kinds of Sons and Spirits to serve there, and that is the theme of Appendix XIII.
w11.026: As his basis for saying that the Ancients of Days and the Master Spirits stay behind in the grand universe, Sadler cites “0:10.12,” but no such paragraph exists. The content he has in mind is found at 0:8.11. That paragraph first says that the Creator Sons take part in the supreme mobilization, then adds that the Ancients of Days and the Seven Master Spirits are “probably eternally fixed as permanent administrators in the grand universe.”
w11.027: 4. Will the Sevenfold Become Tenfold? (orig. pp. 338–339)
w11.028: Drawing on the link between the number ten and the Supreme Being, which Appendix XV will treat, Sadler proposes that God the Sevenfold might become “tenfold” in outer space.
w11.029: Sadler's sketch of the widening from sevenfold to tenfold. Gold boxes mark levels that are new or that change in character
w11.030: At the base of the spiritual series stand the Third-Age Sons and Spirits, the Mixed-Age Sons and Spirits, and the Son-Spirit Creative Trios; the sixth place goes to the completed Supreme Being and the seventh to the eventuating Ultimate. The physical series gains the Associate Master Force Organizers and the Primary Master Force Organizers, and “the Ultimate as Omnipotent” takes a place there too. Sadler's table of the physical series leaves the sixth place unnamed; from the flow of the list it is most likely the completed Almighty Supreme.
w11.031: What draws Sadler's attention is the degree of unification. At present the Supreme Being and the Almighty Supreme are not yet fully joined, but in a tenfold Deity the Supreme would be complete and the finite level unified. The unfinished place would simply move one story higher: the Ultimate as Omnipotent would then stand to God the Ultimate much as the Almighty Supreme now stands to God the Supreme.
w11.033: There is also warrant for placing the force organizers in the physical series. At the superuniverse headquarters the Master Physical Controllers are directed by the Council of Equilibrium, whose high commissioners are sent by the Seven Master Spirits from among the Associate Master Force Organizers [29:4.2]. Even in the present age the two series already work hand in hand.
w11.034: The starting point is the statement that the function of God the Sevenfold “will probably expand” with outer space [0:8.12]; Sadler reads it as an expansion both in quantity and in quality.
w11.035: God the Sevenfold has two series, spiritual ministry and physical control (116:5), and Sadler tentatively proposes a third series of mind.
w11.036: The Creator Sons and Creative Spirits move out into outer space, while the weight of the text favors the Ancients of Days and the Master Spirits remaining in the grand universe (0:8.11).
w11.037: Sadler suggests that God the Sevenfold may become tenfold in outer space, reasoning that the supreme level would then be fully unified and the tension of incompleteness would shift to the ultimate level.
w11.038: The Growth of the Universe Sons and Spirits
w11.039: Appendix XIII, Evolution of Universe Sons and Spirits (pp. 340–347)
w11.040: The two creators of a local universe, the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit, are beings who grow through experience. Sadler gathers what the text says about their nature and their number, then frames a hypothesis: three kinds of Universe Sons and Spirits will serve on the Primary Space Level. They are the Creative Trios, who have perfected a local universe and trinitized a third being; the Mixed-Age Sons and Spirits, born now but destined to become creators in the next age; and the Third-Age Sons and Spirits, who will be born in that next age.
w11.041: 1. The Nature of the Two Creators (orig. pp. 340–341)
w11.042: When the Father and the Son explore the outworking of their union on levels below the infinite, the Michael order, the Creator Sons, comes forth. The text says that in creative power they are “⟦Q 7:6.3⟧potentially equal with God the Father and God the Son⟦/Q⟧” [7:6.3]. Their present function is finite, yet they may hold hidden superfinite capacities. The passage on which Sadler stakes this entire appendix is the following.
w11.044: At the moment a Creator Son is personalized, there is differentiated within the Infinite Spirit the potential of his future consort [17:6.3]. Since the Infinite Spirit can respond without limit, Sadler regards the growth potential of a Creative Spirit as a complement equal in measure to that of her Son.
w11.045: The two creators are also bound to time and space in crossing ways. Within her local universe the Creative Spirit is independent of space but not of time [34:3.3].
w11.047: Sadler reasons that if the two creators should one day achieve a trinitizing union, the being produced would be limited by neither time nor space, at least within an assigned domain. That would be the condition for service on the absonite level.
w11.048: 2. How Many Creator Sons Are There? (orig. pp. 341–342)
w11.049: Each time a Creator Son comes into being, a Creative Spirit is also differentiated, so the number of Sons equals the number of Spirits.
w11.050: Sadler's reasoning on the number of Creator Sons
w11.052: Creator Sons number “more than seven hundred thousand”; elsewhere “nearly one million”
w11.053: The plan of universe organization provides for 700,000 local universes
w11.054: The Unions of Days number exactly 700,000, and no more are being created
w11.055: 700,000 Associate Inspectors; 7 billion Assigned Sentinels (one per local system)
w11.056: The seven superuniverses contain exactly 700,000 local universes
w11.057: Michaels beyond 700,000 will have their first creative experience in outer space
w11.059: The text stops just short of the conclusion. If a sizable number of Michaels are to build their first universes in outer space, then Sons and Spirits with quite different histories will be at work there side by side.
w11.060: The three kinds of Universe Sons and Spirits that Sadler proposes: when each is born and when each first serves as a creator
w11.062: The Master Michael and the Seventh-Stage Creative Spirit
w11.063: The Son-Spirit Creative Trios are the Creator Sons and Creative Spirits who have perfected the seven hundred thousand local universes of this age. Sadler calls them “Trios” because he believes each pair will add one more co-ordinate creator through trinitization.
w11.064: A Master Michael is a creator who has acquired, through experience, the divinity of evolutionary supremacy on top of his Paradise divinity, and who has passed through six stages of sovereignty, from vicegerent sovereignty to the trinitized sovereignty of a universe settled in light and life. The text leaves the seventh only as “⟦Q 21:3.11⟧unrevealed sovereignty⟦/Q⟧” [21:3.11]; Sadler conjectures that it is the stage at which the Son delegates his rule and departs for outer space.
w11.066: His partner is a Creative Spirit who has reached her “unrevealed career.” She passes in turn through her initial differentiation, a preliminary training in which she becomes space cognizant, the physical organization of the local universe, personalization at the time of life creation, elevation to co-sovereignty after the bestowals, and the sixth stage in light and life [17:6]. Sadler pictures the seventh stage as the one in which she becomes fully personal and goes out with her partner into outer space.
w11.068: Sadler's loveliest insight is that the two growths stand at right angles. The Creator Son is a person from the beginning, and his experience is “vertical”: he descends from being one with God in divinity to being one with man in nature. The Creative Spirit begins as a prepersonal focalization of the Infinite Spirit and rises to true personality in the likeness of a Master Spirit; her experience is “horizontal.” The growth that the nature of the one closes off is exactly the growth the other achieves.
w11.069: The vertical growth of the Creator Son and the horizontal growth of the Creative Spirit. Sadler holds that both find joint expression in a third being
w11.070: Together the two growths span almost the whole range of growth open in the present age. Sadler therefore reasons that a pair who have perfected a local universe will have the capacity to express, through trinitization, even this experiential fullness.
w11.072: Early in the history of a local universe the Son and the Spirit bring forth a Bright and Morning Star, Gabriel. It is a complete creative act, unique to each local universe, but it is not a trinitizing union. At that time the Son had not yet made his bestowals and the Spirit was in her fourth stage, so Gabriel expresses only the capacities the two creators then possessed. The text, too, says he is “⟦Q 33:4.2⟧considerably limited in the attributes of Deity⟦/Q⟧” [33:4.2]. Trinitization is another matter. The Father and the Son could bring forth only one Deity equal to themselves, the Conjoint Actor, and by that act the two were joined as the Father-Son [22:7.3]. Sadler holds that if a Master Michael and a seventh-stage Spirit unite in that manner, a co-ordinate offspring will appear and the two will become a “Son-Spirit.”
w11.075: Just as the Infinite Spirit is the “superadditive consequence” of the union of Father and Son [10:2.5], the third being will likely be more than the sum of its parents' attributes. Because it expresses both horizontal and vertical growth, Sadler explains, it may take on an ultimate nature. Each Creative Spirit resembles the Master Spirit of her superuniverse [34:1.3], so the Trios too will fall into seven orders of 100,000 each. This leads into Appendix XIV.
w11.076: 4. Mixed-Age and Third-Age Sons and Spirits (orig. pp. 346–347)
w11.077: Mixed-Age Michaels exist now and continue to be created. Havona is their educational training ground [14:6.27], and on seven worlds of the fourth circuit the reserve corps of Paradise Michaels conducts schools for the pilgrims [26:8.1]. Sadler believes that during this training they take part personally in the growth of the Supreme, not yet as creators but as pre-creator beings. The Mixed-Age Creative Spirits, having no local universe assigned to them, remain in the second stage; they become space cognizant and undergo preliminary training, but their participation is prepersonal [17:6.4].
w11.078: Their creative activity will take place on the Primary Space Level after the present age has closed. The potentials they will work with there are themselves post-supreme, so whatever they gain as creators will likewise bear a post-supreme character. The Third-Age Sons and Spirits will be wholly post-supreme beings, both born and creatively active in the next age. The Paradise divinity they receive will be the same as that of those who came before, and their creative experience will run parallel to what the Mixed-Age group undergoes.
w11.080: Two questions separate the three groups: when were they born, and when do they first serve as creators? Only the Creative Trios have taken part in the growth of the Supreme as creators; the Mixed-Age group has taken part only as pre-creator beings; the Third-Age group appears after that growth is finished. The text goes as far as the fact that there are more than 700,000 Michaels and the belief that the union of Son and Spirit may reach absonite levels. The division into three groups is Sadler's hypothesis.
w11.081: The Creator Son potentially possesses superfinite capacities, and the Creative Spirit is a complement with a growth potential of equal measure.
w11.082: The Creator Son is relatively free of time, the Creative Spirit of space; Sadler expects the being born of their union to surpass both.
w11.083: Creator Sons number more than 700,000 while local universes number exactly 700,000, so the remaining Michaels will build their first universes in outer space.
w11.084: The vertical growth of the Son and the horizontal growth of the Spirit complement each other at right angles and may find expression, as an ultimate nature, in a trinitized third being (21:6.3, 56:7.7).
w11.085: The three groups, Creative Trios, Mixed-Age, and Third-Age, are Sadler's hypothesis, distinguished by the age of their birth and the age in which they first serve as creators.
w11.086: The Widening Influence of the Master Spirits
w11.087: Appendix XIV, Expanding Influence of the Master Spirits (pp. 348–355)
w11.088: The Seven Master Spirits are the first expression of experiential Deity, and when assembled they take in the functioning of Supremacy, Ultimacy, and the Supreme-Ultimate. Sadler finds in them a principle of “divergence-convergence” and foresees it carrying over from the seven cultures of the superuniverses to forty-nine environments in outer space. The backbone of this appendix is threefold: a numerical sketch of administration on the Primary Space Level, the match between the powers of seven and the numbers of the Master Architects, and the “forty-nine viewpoints” of the universal conciliators.
w11.090: The Master Spirits are the first “Deity-creative” act of the Infinite Spirit [9:8.2], and when gathered together they encompass the functional domain of the Supreme-Ultimate in the master universe.
w11.092: Here Sadler proposes the Principle of Divergence-Convergence: what is one divides, and what has divided comes together again to produce something new. Its pattern is the origin of the Third Person of Deity. The absolute personality of the Son is set apart from the personality of infinity (divergence), and the two then unite to give rise to a Third Person unlike either forebear (convergence).
w11.093: Between the Trinity and the Seven Master Spirits this happens along seven lines. Sadler's image is a prism. White light passing through a prism breaks into seven colors, and when the colors are recombined they become white light again. Let the Trinity be the source of the white light and the Master Spirits the seven colors. When that rainbow is gathered once more and cast on the screen of the finite, it becomes the Supreme Being; cast on the screen of the absonite, it becomes God the Ultimate.
w11.094: Sadler's prism analogy: the white light of the Trinity divides into the Seven Master Spirits and is gathered again, as the Supreme Being on the finite screen and as God the Ultimate on the absonite screen
w11.095: On this analogy the Supreme Being and God the Ultimate are the power-personalizations of the Deity values held collectively within the Master Spirits.
w11.096: 2. The Sacred Spheres and the Future of the Superuniverses (orig. pp. 349–351)
w11.098: Sadler reads the outer-space role of the Master Spirits in the three circuits of satellites that encircle Paradise. The seven worlds of the Father are patterned on the seven natures of the Master Spirits, and the secrets of supremacy that preside there concern Supremacy, Ultimacy, and the Supreme-Ultimate [13:2.10]. On the worlds of the Son, the “otherwise-than-personal” beings are being assembled for the new universes of outer space [13:3.2]. The seven worlds of the Spirit, the executive abodes of the Master Spirits, are the Paradise headquarters of the seven superuniverses and also of their “⟦Q 13:4.6⟧correlated segments in outer space⟦/Q⟧” [13:4.6].
w11.099: Each Master Spirit pervades a superuniverse and leaves on it an indelible stamp.
w11.101: This is why the culture of each superuniverse is so distinct, and why the seven superuniverses are at present isolated from one another [15:10.23]. Yet as they become settled in light and life, the boundaries will gradually fade and the grand universe will function as a single whole [117:7.15]. Seven cultures that grew apart are blended again, and here Sadler sees divergence-convergence once more.
w11.102: 3. Sketching the Administration of the Primary Space Level (orig. pp. 351–353)
w11.103: In outer space the Master Spirits are concerned with the segments that correspond to their superuniverses [16:0.11]. Sadler builds on the numbers given in the text to sketch how the Primary Space Level might be administered.
w11.104: Sadler's reasoning on the administration of the Primary Space Level
w11.106: Outer space holds at least 70,000 aggregations of matter, each larger than a superuniverse (31:10.19)
w11.107: All 70,000 lie on the Primary Space Level
w11.108: Seventy Master Architects are assigned to the Primary Space Level (31:9.6)
w11.109: Each Architect is responsible for 1,000 aggregations
w11.110: The 490 of the fifth corps become associate assistants to the seventy of the fourth corps (by analogy with 31:9.11)
w11.111: Each Master Spirit oversees 10,000 aggregations, cared for by ten Architects of the fourth corps and seventy of the fifth
w11.112: The 700,000 Creative Trios of Appendix XIII fall into seven orders. How might they be deployed? A “homogeneous” deployment, gathering each order under the Master Spirit of its own type, would deepen the coloring of each domain. Sadler instead chooses a “heterogeneous” deployment, dividing one seventh of every order among all seven Master Spirits. He gives two reasons: the great current of creation runs toward diversity, and there is a precedent in the Reflective Spirits, one reflecting each of the seven Master Spirits, stationed at every superuniverse capital.
w11.113: Under this scheme each galaxy would be shared among ten Trios, and in each domain the seven inherited natures of the Trios would overlap the seven environments set by the ruling Master Spirit. The result is forty-nine environmental tendencies.
w11.114: Seven “heredities” crossed with seven “environments.” Sadler holds that the seven superuniverse environments will become forty-nine on the Primary Space Level
w11.115: Just as the present Creative Spirits fall into seven orders by resembling their supervising Master Spirits, Sadler argues that the post-supreme Creative Spirits who serve on the Primary Space Level will form forty-nine types.
w11.117: If the post-supreme Sons and Spirits also trinitize at the end of the third age, a “second corps of Creative Trios” in forty-nine orders would serve on the Secondary Space Level. Is there any way to test reasoning that has traveled so far? Sadler points to the numbers of the Master Architects: 70 on the primary level (7 × 10), 490 on the secondary (49 × 10), 3,430 on the tertiary (343 × 10), and 24,010 on the quartan (2,401 × 10). With each space level, seven is multiplied in once more. He says with care that this agreement does not prove his reasoning but shows that it is not without logical footing.
w11.118: 5. The Forty-Nine Viewpoints of the Universal Conciliators (orig. pp. 354–355)
w11.119: A model of forty-nine environments already exists in the present age. The universal conciliators are created in seven orders after the seven natures of the Master Spirits, and every order serves in all seven superuniverses.
w11.121: Sadler also estimates their number. Seven conciliators are created for each Havona servital [25:2.1], and the text mentions servital “⟦Q 24:7.5⟧number 842,842,682,846,782⟦/Q⟧” [24:7.5], so the conciliators may number some seven quadrillion. Orvonton has almost eighteen trillion conciliating commissions, each made up of four members [25:3.15], so the conciliators serving in all the superuniverses come to roughly four hundred trillion. Where are the rest?
w11.123: Sadler reads “universe of universes” as the master universe of the ages to come, and expects this body, with its forty-nine viewpoints, to be put to use in the forty-nine environments of the Primary Space Level. The arithmetic is an estimate built on an estimate, but the text does support the picture that most conciliators have already moved elsewhere. It also says that the personnel of the grand universe is being reorganized in keeping with the energy evolution of outer space [23:4.5].
w11.124: The Seven Master Spirits are the first expression of experiential Deity, and when assembled they together span the whole functional domain of the Supreme-Ultimate (16:1.3).
w11.125: Sadler proposes the Principle of Divergence-Convergence and uses the analogy of a prism to explain how the Master Spirits relate to the Supreme Being and God the Ultimate.
w11.126: The executive worlds of the Spirit serve as headquarters of the superuniverses and of the matching segments of outer space (13:4.6), and the seven divided superuniverse cultures are made one again under the Supreme.
w11.127: Sadler sketches the Primary Space Level with 10,000 aggregations for each Master Spirit; that all 70,000 aggregations lie on that level is his own assumption.
w11.128: A heterogeneous deployment of the Creative Trios crosses seven heredities with seven environments to give forty-nine environments, which fits the powers of seven in the numbers of the Architects.
w11.129: The “forty-nine experiential viewpoints” of the universal conciliators (25:2.4) are an example of this principle already at work.
w11.130: The Master Architects and the Transcendentalers
w11.131: Appendix XV, Master Architects and Transcendentalers (pp. 356–380)
w11.132: The Architects of the Master Universe are the governing corps of the Paradise Transcendentalers, and they number 28,011. By factoring the numbers of their seven corps, Sadler uncovers a pattern woven from one, three, seven, and ten. He then turns to the nature and functions of the Transcendentalers, the uses of the word “absonite,” the three words inceptor, realizer, and consummator, the absonite order in which temporal sequence grows blurred, and the Principle of Organic Consistency, which holds that reality responds like a living organism.
w11.133: 1. The Relations among the Numbers (orig. pp. 356–362)
w11.134: In Appendix VIII Sadler regarded the Architects and Transcendentalers as personalizations of the master universe plan. God's conceiving of a plan and the eventuation of beings to carry it out are two faces of one event. If so, the number of Architects should tell us something about the plan.
w11.136: **One and three.** One belongs to the Infinite and to the Paradise Trinity, undivided in functioning reality. The persons of Deity are three, yet existential Deity in the Trinity is one [10:0.3]. There is no one without the three and no three without the one. Among the Architects there is one senior Architect and there are three Architects of Havona.
w11.137: **Seven.** There are exactly seven ways to combine the three Deities, singly, in pairs, and all together, and so there are seven Master Spirits.
w11.139: That is also why there are seven superuniverses, and why seven appears as a factor in the number of Architects on every one of the five space levels beyond Havona.
w11.140: **Where three and seven meet.** Added, they make ten; multiplied, twenty-one; added and then multiplied by seven, seventy. Sadler takes ten as the number of the Supreme Being. When the three Deities and the Seven Master Spirits brought forth the Reflective Spirits, the Supreme Being functioned uniquely as a creator and brought forth Majeston [17:2.4]; the Architects of the grand universe, too, number three plus seven, ten. Twenty-one is the number of the Paradise satellites and of the Ancients of Days. Seventy is the number of the Trinitized Secrets of Supremacy, for the ten on each world are made up of seven who head the seven divisions and three who represent Trinity Deity [18:1.2]. The major sectors of the seven superuniverses also number seventy.
w11.141: **The powers of seven.** The forty-nine Reflective Spirits resemble the seven Master Spirits seven apiece, and in each superuniverse seven types are stationed to meet that superuniverse's environment. Sadler follows this series on to 343 on the secondary level and 2,401 on the tertiary, and he holds that the 16,807 tendencies the quartan level would produce have no outlet within the master universe. As grounds for this claim that creation moves toward diversity, he points to Havona.
w11.143: 2. The Numbers of the Master Architects (orig. pp. 362–367)
w11.144: The seven corps of Master Architects, their numbers, and Sadler's interpretation (31:9.3–9)
w11.148: The sevenfold expression of Trinity Deity
w11.149: The Supreme Being joined with the seven Master Spirits
w11.150: A second seven laid over the seven natures
w11.152: The fourth interaction of seven with seven
w11.154: The pattern widens from one to three and from three to seven; then, in outer space, ten remains a constant factor while seven is multiplied in once more at each step. Sadler reads the unbroken presence of seven from the third corps onward as a sign that the Master Spirits share in every development of outer space, and the steady presence of ten from the fourth corps onward as a sign that the Supreme Being is active on every outer space level. Outer space, where the two appear together, is where the partnership the text names as “Spirit-Supreme,” one link in the cycle of reality [106:8.12], will find its fullest expression.
w11.155: A remarkable tradition is attached to the total number of Architects. The eventuation of a 28,012th Architect was once attempted, but the being failed to absonitize and its personality was seized by the Universal Absolute.
w11.157: Sadler reads 28,011 as the limit at which the potential for personalization on the absonite level is exhausted, and he insists that these numbers, like the number of the Master Spirits, are no accident. As to why seven stops at the fourth power, he suggests that the Transcendentalers' existence on “⟦Q 30:1.93⟧four ultimate levels of personality activity⟦/Q⟧” [30:1.93] may be related to the four outer space levels. He cautions, however, that these should not be confused with the “seven levels of the absonite” on which the seven corps of Architects function.
w11.159: Sadler assigns the fourth through seventh corps to their domains with confidence, but the text itself only says “we conjecture” and “we likewise infer” about these assignments (31:9.6–9). The quartan corps is linked to the fourth outer universe only “if our former conjectures are valid.” The Architects' domains beyond the superuniverses therefore belong to the revelators' own reasoning, and Sadler's numerical structure rests on that reasoning.
w11.160: 3. The Nature and Functions of the Transcendentalers (orig. pp. 367–371)
w11.162: The Transcendentalers live on the western portion of Paradise [31:8.1] and use a transcendental energy known on Uversa as tranosta [42:2.18]. Their concern is solely with master universe superadministration [31:8.2] and are obedient to the Ultimate [31:8.3]. They function in twelve grand divisions of one thousand working groups, each of seven classes [30:1.93], which Sadler counts as 84,000 classes. Mortals are personal and Transcendentalers superpersonal, yet the two can fellowship. Sadler grants that the Transcendentalers may resemble the “otherwise-than-personal” offspring of the Eternal Son or the Inspired Trinity Spirits in being superpersonal, but since they belong to different groups in the classification of living beings, he does not regard them as kin by descent.
w11.163: Sadler sees God's plan unfolding in three stages. The Architects initiate the plan, the Supreme Creators give it actual shape, and the two together, with experiential Deity, bring its destiny to completion.
w11.165: He insists that the work of the Transcendentalers goes well beyond the making of nebulae, and gives five examples. The first is the design of matter: the stability and elasticity of matter are owed to the “well-nigh infinite wisdom” of the Master Architects [42:9.5]. The second is the design of living things. The unrevealed “⟦Q 36:0.1⟧Architects of Being⟦/Q⟧” [36:0.1], mentioned only once in the text, formulate the plans of life; Sadler states plainly that the text says nothing more, yet he believes they belong among the Transcendentalers. The third is the framework of free choice. The wills of creators and creatures operate within limits set by the Master Architects [118:7.1], which does not abolish free will but defines its range. The fourth is absonite intervention. Personalized Adjusters are the “stabilizers and compensators” of the universe of universes [109:7.2], and during the vorondadek regency on Urantia three uncalled Personalized Adjusters appeared and were among the most active [109:7.7]. The fifth is the absonite ministers who come in the seventh stage of light and life [55:4.10].
w11.167: Sadler takes the English word “absonite” to be a compound joining the first two syllables of “absolute” with the last syllable of “finite.” It is the name for a reality lying between the two, being neither finite nor absolute. He sorts its uses in the text: a level of reality (0:1.12), a quality of function (0:1.10), a degree of Trinity unification (0:9.1), ultimate values (0:2.17), the spirit to be bestowed on the midsoniters (36:4.8), a branch of learning (30:4.31), superconscious insight (117:3.3), the nature of beings (0:12.6), a mode of origin, “absonitize” (31:9.10), and a quality of being.
w11.168: The last use draws Sadler's particular attention. The text says that the Architects possess “⟦Q 31:9.1⟧supernal absonites⟦/Q⟧” [31:9.1]. Just as on finite levels spirit is something added to mind, so for transcendental beings absonity is something added to spirit. Ascending mortals, too, after finishing the Havona career, meet an “absonite differential” that is leveled off only in the seventh stage of the finaliters [44:8.5]. Further, absonite reality has neither beginning nor end and transcends time and space [0:1.12], and its uppermost level touches the absolute [31:9.10]. Sadler infers that its lowest level must touch the finite, and concludes that, as morontia bridges matter and spirit, the absonite bridges the finite and the absolute.
w11.171: Three stages in the actualization of reality (the nine words of 106:8.12 and Sadler's assignments)
w11.174: The created creators, the Supreme Creators
w11.175: Both groups together with experiential Deity
w11.176: Consummation takes place on every level. The text speaks of the Supreme as achieving “⟦Q 117:2.1⟧the consummation of the perfecting future⟦/Q⟧” [117:2.1], and the Absolute Trinity includes the unrevealed “⟦Q 0:12.7⟧Consummator of Universe Destiny⟦/Q⟧” [0:12.7]. To put Sadler's summary in brief: the Transcendentalers prepare, the creators build, and the two together bring the work to its end.
w11.177: 6. The Absonite Order of Sequence (orig. pp. 375–378)
w11.179: From the standpoint of eternity the transcendental appears first, foreseeing the finite; from the standpoint of time it is met at the place where finite evolution comes to its end. Sadler calls this the “before-after” relationship.
w11.180: Here lies a puzzle. If the 28,012th attempt met the Absolute and failed, then the 28,011th Architect, the last to eventuate, ought to serve on the highest level of the absonite. Yet the text says that only the “first-eventuated” senior Architect functions on that level [31:9.3]. The senior Architect would then be both first and last. Sadler interprets this as a sign that finite temporal order does not hold on the absonite level. The citizens of Paradise are conscious of a “⟦Q 11:2.11⟧nontime sequence of events⟦/Q⟧” [11:2.11], and the text also says that sequence may become blurred at the upper limits of the finite.
w11.182: Sadler holds this up against the history of Urantia. The distance by which the incarnation of Machiventa Melchizedek (roughly 1980–1886 B.C.) preceded the life of Jesus is almost equal to the distance by which the appearance of The Urantia Book in 1934–1935 followed it. Both are tied to Michael's bestowal, and so, he suggests, a personality from beyond time may have set in motion both a wave of anticipation and a wave of consequence. This is his own speculation.
w11.183: 7. The Principle of Organic Consistency (orig. pp. 378–380)
w11.184: Sadler tentatively proposes a Principle of Organic Consistency: an act of Deity always calls forth a consistent reaction within the responsive potentials of the level of reality it touches, because reality is not a machine but a living organism.
w11.186: The text portrays the grand universe as “⟦Q 116:7.1⟧a magnificent and responsive living organism⟦/Q⟧” [116:7.1] and compares the nerves, circulation, chemical controls, and adjutant mind of the human body to the grand universe's intelligence circuits, energy lanes, centers of overcontrol, and Supreme Mind [116:7.1–5]. Sadler presses the analogy upward. If the grand universe is an organism being power-personalized in the Supreme, the master universe will be one in the Ultimate, and total reality an absolute organism pervaded by the Infinite. That would explain why every act of divinity must set up a response. On imperfect time-space levels, discord can appear for a season, and that is error and evil.
w11.187: On absolute levels, the Conjoint Creator responds to the action of the Father-Son; the absolute action of the Trinity moves the Deity Absolute, and the Deity Absolute, through the Universal Absolute, moves the Unqualified Absolute. On experiential levels, the Trinity embraces Deity realities, and Deity realities seek personalization.
w11.189: And the principle reaches all the way down to the small steps of human life.
w11.192: The numbers of the Architects, the tradition of the 28,012th attempt, the nature of the Transcendentalers, and the nine words all come from the text. The meaning found in factoring the numbers, the assignment of agents to inception, realization, and consummation, the reading of the senior Architect as both first and last, the symmetry between Melchizedek and The Urantia Book, and the Principle of Organic Consistency are Sadler's interpretations. They are bold, yet each begins from a single line of the text, and for that reason they repay careful reading.
w11.193: The Master Architects are the governing corps of the Transcendentalers and number 28,011; Sadler sees them as personalizations of the master universe plan.
w11.194: The numbers of the seven corps are built from one, three, and seven, from ten where three and seven meet, and from the powers of seven; Sadler reads ten as the mark of the Supreme Being and seven as the mark of the Master Spirits.
w11.195: The failure of the 28,012th attempt shows the limit of absonity (31:9.10), and the place of the senior Architect suggests that temporal sequence does not hold on the absonite level.
w11.196: The Transcendentalers are eventuated beings, neither creators nor creatures, and Sadler holds that they take part in the design of matter and life, the framework of freedom, and even absonite intervention.
w11.197: “Absonite” is used in many senses, and Sadler understands it as a bridge between the finite and the absolute.
w11.198: Inceptors, realizers, and consummators (106:8.12) show an order in which the Transcendentalers prepare, the creators build, and the two finish the work together.
w11.199: The Principle of Organic Consistency is Sadler's proposal, and it reaches as far as the text's statement that when man acts, the Supreme reacts (117:5.6).
